coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 (130–140 bpm), no vert work. You're 45 days out and in taper; Tuesday normally carries a quality workout, but your 30-day avg sleep is 8.28h and yesterday you logged only 6.58h—that's a red flag in a taper phase. Your resting HR dropped to 61 (vs. 65.1 avg), which signals good recovery, but short sleep blunts adaptation and increases injury risk on alpine terrain. Hold the intensity today. Get back to easy, rhythmic running to prime your nervous system without adding load. Save the speed work for Friday if sleep normalizes.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're running 6–8 easy miles; fuel before (oats + banana, 200–250 kcal carbs) and eat a full meal within 90 min post-run. In taper, don't under-fuel thinking less volume = less need—your body is still adapting and glycogen stores matter for the final 45 days. Aim for 6–8g carbs per kg bodyweight daily, with emphasis on the 2–3 hours post-run. Alpine 50Ks demand rock-solid glycogen; a depleted runner dies on the climb to Triglav.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Last night was 6.58h at 94.1% efficiency—acceptable, but below your 30-day target of 8.28h. Tonight, treat sleep like a workout: dim screens by 9:30pm, target 8–8.5h, and keep the bedroom cool (65–67°F). Taper weeks are when the body consolidates fitness; chronic short sleep during this window erodes VO₂ max gains and immune resilience. You travel for work; I know sleep is hard. Prioritize it now more than the previous 20 weeks.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You've logged 5.2 mi yesterday and 5.2 mi so far this week after 32.3 mi last week—a sharp cut that will feel weird and possibly frustrating. That's correct taper math for 45 days out; trust it. The alpine course has 2,500m of vert and sparse aid; your body needs recovery cycles to absorb the peak training stress you absorbed in weeks 16–19. Restlessness is a sign taper is working. Run easy, stay patient, show up rested.
